label: 6 / Mystic Eyes of Death Perception I

lines.japanese:
昼休みになったとたん、今まで授業に一時間も出てなかった男がやってきた。
「よう！
　メシ食おうぜ、メシ！」
　何が嬉しいのか、有彦はとにかく威勢がいい。
「そりゃあメシは当然のように食べるけど、えらく機嫌がいいじゃないか。
なにかあったのか、有彦」
「おう。
ついさっきそこで先輩に昼メシいっしょにどうっすかって声をかけたらさ、断られたんだ」
「………………」
　不思議だ。
　先輩っていうとシエル先輩のことだろうけど、誘いを断られると嬉しいらしい、この友人は。
lines.label: s135
lines.maoEnglish:
The instant lunch break begins, a certain boy who has not attended a single class all morning finally shows up.
“Yo! Lunch, lunch—let’s eat!”
Whatever has him so delighted, Arihiko is bursting with energy.
“Obviously I am going to eat, but you are in a suspiciously good mood. What happened, Arihiko?”
“Yeah. I just asked Ciel if she wanted to have lunch with us, and she turned me down.”
“………………”
Strange.
He clearly means Ciel, but apparently this friend of mine enjoys being turned down.

"Yo Tohno!
Food, let's get some food!"

"Senpai" must be referring to Ciel-senpai, but this guy seems to get happy when his offer is refused.

「あのさ。
有彦、そういう趣味だったっけ」
「いやいや、話は最後まで聞けって。
でな、先輩にどうしてダメなんだよう、って聞いたら『遠野くんが一緒だと、イヤです』だってさ！
　うわははははははははは！
　愉快だろう、遠野！」

lines.label: s135

“Tell me something, Arihiko. Have you always been into that?”

“………………”
Strange.

lines.japanese:
「いやあ、嫌われたもんだな遠野！
　ライバルが減って嬉しいので、今日の昼メシはオレがおごってやろう！」
　ばんばん、とオレの背中を楽しそうに叩く有彦。
「……そっか。
先輩、まだ朝のこと怒ってるのか」
　どうして怒られるのかまったく覚えはないのだけど、たしかに先輩は怒っていたように見えた。
「ほら、行くぞ遠野。
食堂の席は利用客の半分しかないんだからな」
　ずるずる、と有彦は人の腕を強引に引きずっていく。
lines.label: s135
lines.maoEnglish:
“Boy, she really hates you, Tohno! I am so happy to have one less rival that lunch is on me today!”
Arihiko gleefully pounds me on the back.
“I see. Ciel is still angry about this morning.”
I have no idea what I did to deserve it, but she certainly looked angry.
“Come on, Tohno. The cafeteria has half as many seats as it has customers.”
Arihiko seizes my arm and drags me away by force.

lines.japanese:
有彦と席を並べて昼食をとる。
　うちの学校の食堂にはテレビが置かれていて、その日の朝のニュースをビデオで流す、という教育にいいんだか悪いんだか紙一重のことをやっている。
　とりあえず、いま流れているニュースはコンビニエンスストアで酔っ払い客が店員を刺殺した、という、とりあえずむこう三日間ぐらいはコンビニに行きたくなくなるような内容だった。
lines.label: s135
lines.maoEnglish:
Arihiko and I sit down side by side for lunch.
Our cafeteria has a television, and they play recordings of the morning news—one of those ideas poised exactly between educational and appalling.
The current story is about a drunk customer stabbing a convenience-store clerk to death, which is enough to keep me out of convenience stores for the next three days or so.

lines.japanese:
「ぶっそうな世の中だねえ。
無差別に人を殺してる通り魔はいるわ、酔っ払いは人を刺すわ。
こんなんじゃ安心して夜遊びもできねえってもんだよな、ほんと」
　有彦は、わりと真剣にニュースを見ているようだった。
lines.label: s135
lines.maoEnglish:
“What a dangerous world. We have a maniac killing strangers and drunks stabbing people. A guy cannot even go out at night in peace.”
Arihiko seems to be watching the news with surprising seriousness.

「……まあ、たしかに物騒だけど。
とりあえず通り魔事件はもう起きないんだから、いつも通りっていうことじゃないのか」
「そなの？
　通り魔って捕まったんだ？」
「いや、捕まってはいないだろうけど」
―――とりあえず、もうこの世にはいないのだ。
　だから現代の吸血鬼なんていう俗な見出しがテレビに映ることもないし、もう、意味もなく殺される『誰か』がでることもない。

“Really? They catch the guy?”
“No, I don’t think anyone caught him.”
―――At any rate, the one behind it is no longer in this world.
There will be no more lurid MODERN-DAY VAMPIRE headlines on television and no more nameless victims murdered for no reason.

今朝で十人目の死体が発見されたって、いまニュースで流れてるもん」

“Because look. The news says they found the tenth body this morning.”
―――――What?
“Whoa, seriously…? That’s right behind the movie theater I always go to.”

「そんな―――ばかな」
　あいつは。
ネロは、たしかに死んだ。

lines.label: s135
lines.maoEnglish:
“W-wait――――”
I shove Arihiko aside and stare at the television.
There it is.
The news drones on: last night, a tenth victim was claimed by the serial killer.
“That cannot be―――”
He was gone. Nrvnqsr was definitely dead.
So why―――had another body turned up with most of its blood drained away?

「―――まさか」
　考えたくはないけれど。
　ネロがいなくなっても、吸血鬼は、まだ一人残っているじゃないか、志貴――――。

Idiotic as Arihiko’s remark is, it might―――well, have struck the mark.
“―――It cannot be.”
I do not want to consider it.
But even with Nrvnqsr gone, there is still one vampire left, is there not, Shiki――――.

授業が終わって、放課後になった。

　悪い考えばかりが頭の中をかけまわって、気がつけばまわりには誰もいなくなっていたんだから。

No—that is not quite right; before I know it, it is after school.
Dark thoughts chase one another through my head; when I finally look around, everyone else is gone.

Arcueid herself is probably the only one who knows the answer.
I do not know.
Those murders no longer have anything to do with Shiki Tohno.
When I settled things with Nrvnqsr, I returned to this side of the world.
Then―――to go willingly back into that nightmare would be sheer madness.

Just what in the world were you thinking, taking me outside so quickly like that?"
"That's my line……!
What in the world were you thinking!?
Coming into my house like that is just insane!
Are you trying to destroy my life, you idiot……!"
I grit my teeth as I glare at Arcueid.
"I---idiot!?
Are you calling me an idiot!?"

「ばかをばかって言ってんだから、それ以外なにがあるっていうんだばか！
　何か反論があったら聞いてやるから言ってみろ！」
「え───あ、う？」
　とにかくもう、完全に頭にきた。
　こんなに頭にきたのは久しぶりで、怒ったからには相手がなんであれ真っ正面から文句を言わなくちゃ気が済まない。
lines.label: s137
lines.maoEnglish:
“I am calling an idiot an idiot, so what else could I mean, idiot? If you have an argument, let us hear it!”
“Wh───uh?”
I am well and truly furious.
I have not been this angry in years, and now that I am, I will not be satisfied until I tell her exactly what I think, no matter who she is.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"I'm calling an idiot an idiot, so what else is there, idiot!
If you want to argue, I'm listening!"
"Eh----ah, huh?"
I'm completely infuriated.
It's been a while since I've been this mad, and once I'm mad, I have to say everything I want to the person I'm mad at, no matter who it is.

lines.japanese:
「なによ、わたしは志貴に会いに来ただけじゃない。
そんなに怒られるようなコトはしてないわ！」
「……ちょっと待て。
会いにきただけって、アルクェイド、おまえ本気で言ってるのか」
「だって、わたし別におかしなコトは言ってないわ。
志貴の妹さんには志貴の目のことも、わたしのコトもちゃんと黙っててあげてたんだから」
「そんなのは当然だ。
そんな事まで口にしてたらこうして話なんかしてない。
ためらわずにあの場で屋敷の外にほうりだしてた」
lines.label: s137
lines.maoEnglish:
“All I did was come to see you, so why are you this angry? I did nothing to deserve it!”
“Wait, you only came to see me? Arcueid, are you serious?”
“I did not say anything strange. I even kept quiet about your eyes and about myself when I talked to your sister.”
“Of course you did. If you had mentioned any of that, we would not be standing here talking. I would have thrown you off the estate on the spot.”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Hey, I just came to see you.
I didn't do anything to make you mad!"
"…… Wait.
Are you serious, Arcueid?
You only came to see me?"
"I didn't even say anything weird.
I didn't say anything to your sister about your eyes or about me or anything."
"Of course.
If you did, we wouldn't be talking like this.
I would not have hesitated and thrown you out if you did."

lines.japanese:
「……わっかんないなあ。
それじゃなんでそんなに怒ってるのよ、貴方は」
「そっちがあんまりにも考えなしだからだろっ！
　いいか、おまえは居るだけで目立つんだ。
この際だから言っておくけど、おまえはもう少し自分が厄介な存在なんだって気がついたほうがいいぞ……！」
　と、とりあえず言いたい事を全部口にした。
　そうなるとスッキリとして冷静になれるのだけど、言われたい放題のアルクェイドは当然のようにスッキリしない。
　アルクェイドは猫のようにむーっと、不機嫌そうに睨んでくる。
lines.label: s137
lines.maoEnglish:
“I do not get it… then why are you so angry?”
“Because you never think anything through!
Listen, you stand out just by being there. While we are at it, you need to realize that your very presence causes trouble…!”
There, I have finally said everything I wanted to say.
With it all out of my system, my head clears, though Arcueid, having endured the entire tirade, is naturally no happier.
She glares at me with a catlike pout.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… I don't get it.
Then why are you so mad?"
"That's because you don't ever think!
Look, you already stand out just being here.
I'll say it now, but you should realize that just by being here you cause trouble……!"
For the time being, I said it all.
Getting it all out of my system calms me down, but obviously Arcueid isn't so calm.
Looking like a cat, she stares at me ill-temperedly.

lines.japanese:
「―――なによ、かってなことばっかり言って。
だいたい居るだけで目立つってどうしてよ。
わたし、外見は人間と変わらないでしょう？」
「だから、美人は居るだけで目立つものなんだって。
人間であるかどうかなんて関係ない」
　きっぱりと言い返す。
　あんまりにあっさりした返答だったからか、アルクェイドもそっか、とあっさり納得したようだ。
lines.label: s137
lines.maoEnglish:
“―――You are the one saying whatever you please. And why would I stand out just by being there? I look no different from a human.”
“Because beautiful women stand out wherever they are. Whether you are human has nothing to do with it.”
I answer without hesitation.
Perhaps because the answer comes so readily, Arcueid accepts it just as readily.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"----What, saying things like that… What do you mean I stand out?
Don't I look like any other human?"
"No, beautiful women always stand out.
It doesn't have anything to do with being human."
I answer directly.
I answer so flatly that Arcueid understands flatly, too.

lines.japanese:
「───まあ、こっちも言い過ぎた。
こういう修羅場っていうのは初めてだったから、気が動転してたんだ」
「……別にいいよ。
悪かったのはわたしの方みたいだから」
　アルクェイドはやけに素直にうなずいた。
　なんか、それはそれで裏がありそうで恐いな、と思ってしまう自分が後ろめたい。
　……そもそも、どうしてアルクェイドはうちにやってきたりしたんだろう……？
lines.label: s137
lines.maoEnglish:
“───Anyway, I went too far. I have never been caught in crossfire like that before, and I panicked.”
“It is fine. It sounds like I was the one at fault.”
Arcueid nods with disconcerting meekness.
I feel guilty for finding even that suspicious.
But why did she come to my house in the first place?

"---Well, I said too much.
It was the first time that's happened to me, so I kind of panicked."
"…… That's okay.
It seems like I was the one to blame."
Arcueid nods meekly.
I feel a little guilty because I think there's something more to it than that.
…… In the first place, why did she come to my house……?

「ところでさ、どうしてうちに来たりしたんだよ。
……まあ、こっちもおまえに話があったから、ちょうど良かったっていえば良かったんだけど」
「そうなの？
　わたしはただ、志貴はどうしてるのかなって様子を見に来ただけなんだけど」
「……そうか。
頼むから、次はどこか目立たないところでこっそり見に来てくれ。
できるだけ誰にもみつからないようにな」
　……なんだか、どっと疲れた。
lines.label: s137
lines.maoEnglish:
“By the way, why did you come to my house? I suppose the timing worked out, since I needed to talk to you too.”
“Oh, you did? I only came by to see how you were doing.”
“I see… next time, please come see me somewhere inconspicuous. Try not to let anyone find you.”
All at once, I feel exhausted.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Anyway, why did you come over?
…… Well, I wanted to talk to you, too, so I guess it's a good thing."
"Really?
I was just… wondering how you were doing, so I swung by to see you."
"…… I see.
Next time, please do so in a different place.
And as stealthily as possible, too."
…… I'm worn out.

lines.japanese:
「―――ともかくだ、真剣に話したいことがある。
ここじゃ落ち着かないから場所を変えたいんだけど、いいか？」
「いいけど―――話ってなによ」
「すぐにわかる。
……そうだな、そろそろ人気もなくなるし、公園あたりがいいかもしれない」
　行くよ、と声をかけて歩き始める。
　アルクェイドは首をかしげながら、大人しく後についてきた。
lines.label: s137
lines.maoEnglish:
“―――Anyway, I need to talk to you about something serious. I cannot talk freely here, so can we go somewhere else?”
“All right, but―――what do you want to talk about?”
“You will see. It should be empty soon, so the park might be best.”
I tell her to come along and start walking.
Arcueid tilts her head, then obediently follows.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"----Anyway, I want to have a serious talk.
I want to talk about it somewhere else since I feel uneasy here, so is that okay?"
"Sure----but talk about what?"
"You'll see.
…… There'll be less people around, so let's go more towards the middle of the park."
Telling her to come on, I start walking.
Tilting her head in curiosity, she follows me obediently.

―――夜は始まったばかりだ。
　いや、正確に言うのなら、アルクェイドが出歩いているとしたら日中よりは夜、それも深夜に近い時間帯だろう。
「……やっぱり街を中心に探しまわったほうが効率的か」
　……考えたくないが、吸血鬼事件の犠牲者はたいてい路地裏で発見される。
　アルクェイドを―――いや、まだ続いている吸血鬼殺人の犯人を探すのなら、街を地道に探しまわるしかないだろう。
lines.label: s138
lines.maoEnglish:
―――The night has only just begun.
More precisely, if Arcueid is out at all, she is more likely to roam at night than during the day—probably closer to midnight.
“I will have better odds if I concentrate on downtown.”
I do not like thinking about it, but most victims of the vampire killings are found in back alleys.
If I want to find Arcueid―――no, whoever is still committing those murders, I will have to search the city street by street.

lines.maoEnglish:
“―――Damn it. What the hell am I doing?”
Unable to make sense of my own feelings, I curse and start running aimlessly again.

lines.japanese:
「――――――はあ」
　どさり、とガードレールに腰を下ろす。
　あれから数時間。
　あてもなく探しまわってみたはいいが、アルクェイドの姿は影も形も見当たらない。
lines.label: s138
lines.maoEnglish:
“――――――Haaah.”
I drop heavily onto a guardrail.
Hours have passed.
I have searched everywhere without the faintest idea where to look, and found no trace of Arcueid.

lines.mirrorMoon:
------*sigh*
I sit down on the guard rail.
It's been several hours already.
I looked around aimlessly, and I didn't even catch a single glimpse of Arcueid.

　そりゃあ街の中でなんのアテもなく人を見つけ出すのがどれだけ困難かわかってはいたけど、アイツにかぎってはあっさりと見付かるって、心のどこかで楽観していた。
「どこいったんだよ、アイツ……」

　別にアイツには吸血鬼殺人の話を聞くだけなのに、会えないとわかると、ひどく―――
lines.label: s138
lines.maoEnglish:
“Damn it…”
I am so damn frustrated.
I knew how nearly impossible it would be to find one person in a city without a lead, yet some part of me had assumed that she, of all people, would just turn up.
“Where the hell did she go…?”
Why, I wonder.
All I need from her is an answer about the vampire killings, yet now that I cannot find her, I feel so terribly―――

　いいかげん時刻も午前零時になろうとしている。

「……………」

“Forget it. I am done with this.”
I rise from the guardrail and start walking.
It is nearly midnight. I cannot keep wasting my time searching for Arcueid.
“……………”
Still, after coming this far, I might as well look a little longer.
One last place; if she is not there, I will go back to the estate.

Grumbling, I step into the park.

lines.maoEnglish:

“That is strange. I know I sent a dream demon to you.”

“A reward―――? I can do without that kind of reward; what goes through the minds of vampires, pulling a tasteless stunt like this?”
I shrug in exasperation.
For some reason, that only makes Arcueid glare at me more fiercely.
“You are so mean, Shiki. Fine, I am not human anyway—so there.”
She turns away in a huff and marches off.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"That's not it at all.
I sent it as thanks for defeating Nrvnqsr.
I really am grateful to you, I thought you'd be extremely happy."
"As thanks?---I'll pass on that kind of thanks.
Having that kind of poor taste, just what are vampires thinking?"
I slump my shoulders.
I don't know what she's mad about, but she looks at me with a dissatisfied expression.
"What's that all about, you meanie?
I know I'm not human."
She turns away, then starts walking off.

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: Arcueid says the familiar shows a dream in the form its subject desires; Shiki later calls it his desire. Neither line ranks that desire above every other desire. mirror moon adds 'the most' and then repeats 'greatest,' turning an embarrassing manifestation into a definitive hierarchy of Shiki's wants just before the text explains that the immature familiar freely embellishes them.

“It has nothing to do with you, Shiki, so leave me alone.”
She turns away with a petulant toss of her head and starts walking again.
This is getting ridiculous.
It seems our silent wandering is about to begin all over again.

　心臓の音が、やけに近くで聞こえた。
　まだ夜も深くないという時間。
　賑やかな繁華街のただ中にいるのに、自分以外の人の気配が、まったく感じられなくなった。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
―――Thump.
My heartbeat sounds unnaturally close.
The night is still young.
I stand in the heart of a bustling entertainment district—yet I can no longer sense anyone here but myself.
lines.mao_english:
―――Thump.
My heartbeat sounds unnaturally close.
The night is still young.
I stand in the heart of a bustling entertainment district—yet I can no longer sense anyone here but myself.
lines.mirrorMoon:
---Thump.
The sound of my heartbeat is awfully close.
It's not even real late at night.
Even though I'm in the midst of a bustling shopping district, I can't sense anyone besides myself.
lines.mirror_moon:
---Thump.
The sound of my heartbeat is awfully close.
It's not even real late at night.
Even though I'm in the midst of a bustling shopping district, I can't sense anyone besides myself.

lines.japanese:
―――ドクン。
　メガネ―――メガネを早くかけなくっちゃ。
　そうしないと、厭なものを見てしまう。
　今まで視えていたものなんて入り口にすぎないぐらいの闇を、見ることになってしまう。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
―――THUMP.
My glasses―――I have to put them back on.
Otherwise I will see something hideous.
A darkness so vast that everything my eyes have shown me before was only its threshold.
lines.mao_english:
―――THUMP.
My glasses―――I have to put them back on.
Otherwise I will see something hideous.
A darkness so vast that everything my eyes have shown me before was only its threshold.
lines.mirrorMoon:
---THUMP.
My glasses---I have to put on my glasses.
If I don't do that, I'll see terrible things.

I'll see something so terrible that everything I've seen so far would be nothing in comparison to it.
lines.mirror_moon:
---THUMP.
My glasses---I have to put on my glasses.
If I don't do that, I'll see terrible things.

I'll see something so terrible that everything I've seen so far would be nothing in comparison to it.

lines.japanese:
―――ど、く、ん。
　でも体が動かない。
　ツギハギだらけのセカイを視る裸眼は、魅了されたように、アルクェイドが入っていった路地裏を、壁越しに見つめている。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
―――Th—ump.
But my body will not move.
My naked eyes see a world stitched together from broken pieces and, as though enthralled, stare through the wall into the alley Arcueid entered.
lines.mao_english:
―――Th—ump.
But my body will not move.
My naked eyes see a world stitched together from broken pieces and, as though enthralled, stare through the wall into the alley Arcueid entered.
lines.mirrorMoon:
---Th, u, mp.
But my body won't move.
My eyes that can see this patchwork world look towards that alley in fascination.

lines.japanese:
「───────」
　唐突に、音が消えた。
　人の気配も、
　風の音も、
　土の匂いも。
　すべて、ピタリと凍りついた。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“───────”
Without warning, all sound ceases.
Every human presence,
the sound of the wind,
even the smell of earth.
Everything freezes in place.
lines.mao_english:
“───────”
Without warning, all sound ceases.
Every human presence,
the sound of the wind,
even the smell of earth.
Everything freezes in place.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"------"
Suddenly, sounds vanish.
And the presence of other people,
the sound of the wind,
and the smell of the dirt.
All of it freezes.
lines.mirror_moon:
"------"
Suddenly, sounds vanish.
And the presence of other people,
the sound of the wind,
and the smell of the dirt.
All of it freezes.

lines.japanese:
絶対零度の月の下。
　壁のむこうで、何か、異質な音がしている。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
Beneath a moon at absolute zero.
An alien sound comes from beyond the wall.
lines.mao_english:
Beneath a moon at absolute zero.
An alien sound comes from beyond the wall.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Under the frozen moon.
A bizarre noise sounds from the other side of the wall.
lines.mirror_moon:
Under the frozen moon.
A bizarre noise sounds from the other side of the wall.

lines.japanese:
見えるはずがないし、
　音なんて聞こえてこない。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
There is no possible way to see it,
no sound could possibly reach me.
lines.mao_english:
There is no possible way to see it,
no sound could possibly reach me.
lines.mirrorMoon:
No way I can see it,
I can't hear anything.
lines.mirror_moon:
No way I can see it,
I can't hear anything.

lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish: ──────Shhk, squelch
lines.mao_english: ──────Shhk, squelch
lines.mirrorMoon: ------A sickening sound
lines.mirror_moon: ------A sickening sound

lines.japanese:
なのに、視えた。
　死と死が衝突する音を、この眼が確かに視た。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
And yet I see it.
These eyes unmistakably see the sound of death colliding with death.
lines.mao_english:
And yet I see it.
These eyes unmistakably see the sound of death colliding with death.
lines.mirrorMoon:
But I can see it.
My eyes definitely see the sound of death and death crashing.
lines.mirror_moon:
But I can see it.
My eyes definitely see the sound of death and death crashing.

lines.japanese:
「ぐ――――」
　視界が朱い。
　なんで―――見えないはずのものの、『死』を視てしまっているんだ、この目は。
「――――」
　メガネ。
メガネをかけないと、頭がどうにかなってしまう。
　喉元までせりあがった嘔吐感をこらえながら、震える手でメガネをかけなおした。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ghh――――”
My vision floods crimson.
Why are these eyes seeing the death of something that should be invisible―――?
“――――”
My glasses. If I don’t put them on, I’ll lose my mind.
Holding back the vomit rising into my throat, I put my glasses back on with a trembling hand.
lines.mao_english:
“Ghh――――”
My vision floods crimson.
Why are these eyes seeing the death of something that should be invisible―――?
“――――”
My glasses. If I don’t put them on, I’ll lose my mind.
Holding back the vomit rising into my throat, I put my glasses back on with a trembling hand.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Gah----"
My vision turns crimson.
Why---do my eyes see "death", something that shouldn't be able to be seen?
"----"
My glasses.
I have to put on my glasses or I'll go insane.
I hold back the rising gorge in my throat and use my shaking hand to put on my glasses.
lines.mirror_moon:

"----"

lines.japanese:
音と光が戻る。
　気をしっかりと持ってあたりを見渡せば、繁華街に異状はない。
　雑多な喧騒と、まわりを歩いていく人々の姿。
　飾り付けられた店のショーウィンドウの明るさや、道路を走る自動車のエンジン音が溢れている。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
Sound and light return.
When I force myself to look around, nothing is wrong with the entertainment district.
Pedestrians stream through the familiar din.
Decorated shop windows blaze with light, and car engines fill the road with noise.
lines.mao_english:
Sound and light return.

Pedestrians stream through the familiar din.
Decorated shop windows blaze with light, and car engines fill the road with noise.
lines.mirrorMoon:
Sound and light return.
Now that I'm calm, I glance around and see nothing out of the ordinary in the shopping district.
The bustling of many people passing by.
The brightness of a store's decorated show window and the sound of rushing car engines.
lines.mirror_moon:
Sound and light return.

The bustling of many people passing by.
The brightness of a store's decorated show window and the sound of rushing car engines.

lines.japanese:
「はあ――はあ、はあ―――」
　呼吸がうまく出来ない。
　メガネをかけていても、どこか視界のすみにさっきの『死』が残っていそうで、気持ち悪い。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Hah――hah, hah―――”
I can’t breathe properly.
Even through the glasses, the thought that some remnant of that death may still lurk at the edge of my vision sickens me.
lines.mao_english:
“Hah――hah, hah―――”
I can’t breathe properly.
Even through the glasses, the thought that some remnant of that death may still lurk at the edge of my vision sickens me.
lines.mirrorMoon:
I'm panting excessively.
I can hardly breathe.
Even though I put my glasses back on, I can still feel a lingering remnant of that "death" and it makes me sick.
lines.mirror_moon:
I'm panting excessively.
I can hardly breathe.
Even though I put my glasses back on, I can still feel a lingering remnant of that "death" and it makes me sick.

lines.japanese:
「アル――クェイド……？」
　路地裏から出てきたアルクェイドは、俺以上に息をきらして、おぼつかない足取りだった。
「―――志貴……そっか、まだ残ってたんだ」
　はあはあ、と肩で息をしながら、ゆらりと、アルクェイドは俺の横をすり抜けていく。
　体をかすかにゆらして、まるで病人のように、弱々しく歩いていく。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Ar――cueid…?”
Arcueid stumbles out of the alley, breathing even harder than I am, her steps unsteady.
“―――Shiki, so you are still here”
Her shoulders heaving with every breath, she sways past me.
Her body rocks faintly as she walks, frail as an invalid.
lines.mao_english:
“Ar――cueid…?”
Arcueid stumbles out of the alley, breathing even harder than I am, her steps unsteady.
“―――Shiki, so you are still here”
Her shoulders heaving with every breath, she sways past me.
Her body rocks faintly as she walks, frail as an invalid.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Ar--cueid……?"
Arcueid walks out from the alley with faltering steps, breathing even harder than I am.
"---Shiki…… I see, you were, still here."
Shoulders heaving up and down, she passes by me.
Her body sways back and forth, and she walks weakly as if she was sick.

lines.japanese:
―――正直、こっちだって吐き気が止まっていない。
　けど、あんなに苦しげなアルクェイドを前にして、そんな生易しいコトはいってられない。
「待てよ、一体どうしたんだおまえ……！」
「大丈夫よ。
すこし疲れただけだから、かまわないで。
―――志貴には、ぜんぜん関係がないんだから」
「ばか、疲れているなら休め！
　そんな青い顔して、ぜんぜん大丈夫そうじゃないじゃないか!」
　ハア、とまだうまく出来ない呼吸を押さえつけながら、アルクェイドの腕を掴む。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
―――To be honest, my own nausea has not eased.
But beside Arcueid’s obvious suffering, it seems too trivial to mention.
“Wait, what happened to you…!?”
“I’m fine. Just a little tired, so leave me alone. ―――It has nothing at all to do with you, Shiki.”
“Idiot, if you’re tired, then rest! You’re white as a sheet—you don’t look fine at all!”
Still fighting for breath, I catch her by the arm.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
---To be honest, I still feel nauseous.
But, seeing Arcueid in pain like that makes me bear it.
"Wait, what in the world……!"
"I'm fine, just a little tired so don't worry.
---It really doesn't concern you Shiki."
"Idiot, if you're tired then rest!
With such a pale face, you can't be fine!"
Even as I breathe shallowly for air, I grab Arcueid's arm.

lines.japanese:
「……なによ。
そういう志貴だって、今にも倒れそうな顔してる」
「俺のはただの貧血だよ。
人のことを気にしてる余裕があるなら、自分の体を気遣ってやれよ」
「―――いいのよ。
どうせ気遣っても無駄なんだから」
　アルクェイドの呼吸は、本当に、切ないぐらいに弱々しい。
「まさか―――おまえ、あの時の傷―――」
　治ってないのか、とは聞けなかった。
　それは、俺を庇って出来た傷だからだ。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Look who’s talking. You look ready to collapse yourself.”
“Mine’s just anemia. If you have enough energy to worry about me, use it to look after yourself.”
“―――There’s no point. Looking after myself won’t change anything.”
Arcueid’s breathing is heartbreakingly weak.
“Don’t tell me―――those wounds from before―――”
I cannot ask whether they have failed to heal.
She received those wounds protecting me.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Hey now.
You say that, but you look like you'll collapse too."
"It's just my anemia.
If you have time to worry about me, worry about your health."
"---It's fine.
There's no point in worrying about it anyway."
Her breathing really is weak.
"Don't tell me---that wound from that time---"
It hasn't healed?
But I can't bring myself to finish.
It's because she got it saving me.

lines.japanese:
「―――――」
　アルクェイドは俯いたまま答えない。
　それは、否定ではなく肯定の意味合いだ。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“―――――”
Arcueid keeps her head lowered and says nothing.
Her silence is an admission.
lines.mao_english:
“―――――”
Arcueid keeps her head lowered and says nothing.
Her silence is an admission.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"-----"
She doesn't answer and looks down.
That is affirmation rather than disagreement.
lines.mirror_moon:
"-----"
She doesn't answer and looks down.
That is affirmation rather than disagreement.

lines.japanese:
「ばっ――――そんな体で何してるんだよ！
　傷が治るまで大人しくしてないとダメじゃないか！
「大人しく、してるつもり、なんだけどな」
「全然してないだろっ！
　いくらおまえが人間離れしてるからって、そんな体でさっきは何をしてたっていうんだよ、一体―――」
　……放っておけない。
　やっぱり、俺はこのどうしようもなく手のかかるヤツを、放っておけない。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“You id――――what are you doing in that condition? You should be resting until your wounds heal!”
“I thought I was taking it easy…”
“You haven’t taken it easy at all! I don’t care how inhuman you are—what were you doing back there in that state―――”
I can’t leave her alone.
No matter what, I can’t abandon this hopelessly troublesome woman.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Stu----What are you doing in your condition!?
You have to take it easy until you're fully healed!"
"I do think I'm, taking it, easy."
"No you're not!
Even if you are at a level beyond humans, what in the world were you doing earlier in your condition---"
…… I just can't leave her be.

I knew it.
I just can't leave this person who's always getting into trouble alone.

lines.japanese:
「黙ってないで答えろ。
おまえが話してくれるまで、俺はおまえから離れないからな……！」
　ぐっ、とアルクェイドの両肩を強く掴む。
　アルクェイドは俯いたまま、こくん、とかすかに頷いたように見えた。
「……もう。
わりとしつこいのね、貴方って。
いいわ、それじゃ場所を変えましょう」
　アルクェイドはこちらの腕を払って、ゆるやかに歩き始めた。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Answer me. I’m not leaving your side until you tell me what’s going on…!”
I seize Arcueid by both shoulders.
Still looking down, she seems to give the faintest nod.
“Honestly, you’re awfully persistent. Fine. Let’s go somewhere else.”
She brushes my arms away and sets off at an easy pace.
lines.mao_english:

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Don't be silent and answer me.
Until you tell me, I won't go away……!"
I grasp both of her shoulders.
Still looking down, she gives a slight nod.
"…… Geez, you really are persistent.
Fine, let's go somewhere else to talk."
Releasing herself, she waveringly starts to walk away.

lines.japanese:
公園に戻ってきた。
　アルクェイドは歩いているうちに体力が回復したのか、すっかり元気な顔になってしまってる。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
We return to the park.
Perhaps the walk has restored her strength, because Arcueid looks perfectly healthy again.
lines.mao_english:
We return to the park.
Perhaps the walk has restored her strength, because Arcueid looks perfectly healthy again.
lines.mirrorMoon:
We come to the park.

lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「さて。
それじゃあ志貴のお望み通り、なんでも話してあげようじゃない」
　さっきまでの弱々しさはどこに行ったのか、アルクェイドはとても偉そうだ。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Well then. Since you insisted, I suppose I’ll tell you anything you want to know.”
All trace of her earlier weakness is gone; Arcueid looks unbearably smug.
lines.mao_english:
“Well then. Since you insisted, I suppose I’ll tell you anything you want to know.”

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Well, as you wish, Shiki, I'll talk about whatever you want."
I don't know where her previous weakness went, but she looks really haughty all of a sudden.
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「……それじゃ聞くけど、さっきのヤツはなんだったんだ。
おまえは吸血鬼って言ってたけど、アレがおまえの標的だったのか？」
「違うわ。
たしかにアレも処刑する対象だけど、あんな死者を塵に還すことが目的じゃない。
アレはわたしの『敵』の下僕だから始末しただけ。
　あんなのでもね、ほっとくと人を殺して力を蓄えられてしまうから」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Then tell me what that thing was. You called it a vampire, but was it your target?”
“It was not my target, though it was marked for execution. My purpose is not to reduce every member of the Dead to dust. It was a servant of my ‘enemy,’ so I disposed of it.
Even something like that will kill people and gather strength if left alone.”
lines.mao_english:

Even something like that will kill people and gather strength if left alone.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Then I'll ask, but just what was that guy earlier?
You said he was a vampire, was he what you were after?"
"No, he certainly is part of my target, but putting The Dead back into the grave isn't my goal.
I only got him because he was a minion of my 'enemy'.
If I left him alone, he would kill more people to increase his power."

“So this ‘enemy’ is the one behind the killings around town?”

アレは死体に寄生するハイチの白蛇のことだけど、動く死体っていったらゾンビが有名なんでしょ？」

lines.maoEnglish:
“The Dead are much the same.
Listen. If a vampire drains someone’s blood and sends some of its own blood back into the victim, that person remains in this world despite being dead.
We call them the Dead, and they are the common familiars of vampires.
Though perhaps ‘zombie’ would make more sense to you, Shiki. Strictly speaking that refers to the Haitian white serpent said to inhabit a corpse, but ‘zombie’ is the famous word for a walking corpse, isn’t it?”
―――Well, that does give me a much clearer picture.

lines.mirrorMoon:
"The Dead are like that.
When humans have their blood sucked by a vampire, they can also receive some of the vampire's blood.
They die, but remain in this world as a servant of the vampire.
They are called The Dead and they are like the vampire's familiars.
Ah, maybe it's easier to understand if I use the word zombie.
It's closer to the voodoo belief in Haiti where the white serpent-god Damballah is invoked to control a dead body, but let's just say a dead body that moves is a zombie, okay?"
---Yeah, I can visualize it better that way.

　もともとわたし達と違って目的がないくせに“不老不死”になった彼らは、不老不死を手にいれた瞬間にあらゆる物欲がなくなってしまったのよ。

lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“―――Amusements―――what the hell does that mean? You kill humans for fun and turn their corpses into toys…!?”
“I won’t deny it.
To vampires, amusement is as necessary as breathing. Though they came from humanity—a species bound to the cycle of life—they drew close, however imperfectly, to ageless immortality, and boredom became their greatest enemy.
Unlike us, they had no purpose beyond attaining immortality; the instant they achieved it, every material desire vanished.
Immortality had been their only goal, so perhaps that result was inevitable.”

lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“That became enough for them—and that was the problem.
An existence without purpose has no meaning. Once a living being recognizes itself as worthless―――as something that has stopped, there is no longer any value in its continued existence. Immortality is merely another name for death.
They gradually wore away, and so began inventing diversions. They needed to reassure themselves that they were alive, that pleasure remained to them.
―――That was the birth of the vampire aristocracy.”

「さて、ここで話は前後するけど、死徒というものは元は人間なの。
　魔術を究めてその果てに吸血鬼となった稀なケースもあるけど、大部分は血を吸われた人間が死徒になる。
　死徒はたしかに不老不死だけれど、彼らは永久機関じゃないわ。
だからたえず他者から命を吸い上げないと不老不死ではいられない。
　前に、彼らは不完全な不老不死だと言ったでしょ？
　死徒は結局、人間という捕食対象がいないと“不老不死”ではいられない」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Now, this takes us backward a little, but Dead Apostles were originally human.
A rare few became vampires after mastering magecraft, but most were humans whose blood was taken.
Dead Apostles truly are ageless and immortal, but they are not perpetual motion machines. They must constantly drain life from others to preserve that immortality.
I told you theirs was imperfect, remember? Without humans to prey upon, a Dead Apostle cannot retain immortality.”
lines.mao_english:
“Now, this takes us backward a little, but Dead Apostles were originally human.
A rare few became vampires after mastering magecraft, but most were humans whose blood was taken.
Dead Apostles truly are ageless and immortal, but they are not perpetual motion machines. They must constantly drain life from others to preserve that immortality.
I told you theirs was imperfect, remember? Without humans to prey upon, a Dead Apostle cannot retain immortality.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Well, we'll change the topic, but the Dead Apostles were originally human.
There are a few cases where they became vampires through their own magical research, but the majority of them were humans who had their blood sucked.
They are immortal, but they can't last forever.
They can only be immortal if they drink the blood of others.
Didn't I say their immortality was imperfect?
If they can't feed on humans then their immortality is gone."
lines.mirror_moon:
"Well, we'll change the topic, but the Dead Apostles were originally human.
There are a few cases where they became vampires through their own magical research, but the majority of them were humans who had their blood sucked.
They are immortal, but they can't last forever.
They can only be immortal if they drink the blood of others.

If they can't feed on humans then their immortality is gone."

lines.japanese:
「……ちょっと待った。
それ、おかしいよ。
　そうなると死徒っていうのは不老不死でいるために人間から血を吸うけど、そのたびに新しい死徒ってのを生み出してるって事になるじゃないか」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Wait. That doesn’t make sense.
If Dead Apostles drink human blood to remain immortal, but each feeding creates another Dead Apostle, then their numbers should multiply every time.”
lines.mao_english:
“Wait. That doesn’t make sense.
If Dead Apostles drink human blood to remain immortal, but each feeding creates another Dead Apostle, then their numbers should multiply every time.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… Wait a minute, isn't that odd?
In order to become immortal they drink the blood of humans, but doesn't that mean new Dead Apostles will be born every time they do that?"
lines.mirror_moon:
"…… Wait a minute, isn't that odd?
In order to become immortal they drink the blood of humans, but doesn't that mean new Dead Apostles will be born every time they do that?"

lines.japanese:
「そうなんだけど、ここからが複雑でね。
　血を吸われた人間は死んでしまう。
けどこの時、死徒が自らの血をその死体に残しておくと、殺された人間は死にきれなくなる。
　この死にきれない遺体が墓場の中で数年たって、脳が腐敗して魂が肉体に完全に“固定”した状態になると屍食鬼（グール）になるの。
　グールになれるのは百人に一人ぐらいの割合だから、なにも全ての人間が“残れる”わけではないわ。
　……まあ、中には生まれた時から上位種へステップアップできる資格をもっている人間がいて、そういう人たちは即座に新種の吸血種になるんだけど、それは本当に稀だから論外ね。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“That’s where it becomes complicated.
A human whose blood is taken dies. But if the Dead Apostle leaves some of its own blood in the corpse, the victim cannot finish dying.
After this half-dead body spends several years in the grave—until the brain decays and the soul becomes completely ‘fixed’ to the flesh—it turns into a ghoul.
Only about one person in a hundred can become a ghoul, so most victims do not remain.
A very few people are born qualified to advance directly into a higher species and become a new kind of vampiric creature at once, but this is so rare we can ignore it.”
lines.mao_english:
“That’s where it becomes complicated.
A human whose blood is taken dies. But if the Dead Apostle leaves some of its own blood in the corpse, the victim cannot finish dying.
After this half-dead body spends several years in the grave—until the brain decays and the soul becomes completely ‘fixed’ to the flesh—it turns into a ghoul.
Only about one person in a hundred can become a ghoul, so most victims do not remain.
A very few people are born qualified to advance directly into a higher species and become a new kind of vampiric creature at once, but this is so rare we can ignore it.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"That's true, but things get complex from here.
The people who have their blood sucked die.
But at that time, if the Dead Apostles place a little of their blood inside the corpse, the body cannot die.
Those bodies that were unable to die stay a number of years in the grave and when the brain decays and the soul is "fixated" in the body, they become a flesh-eating corpse (ghoul).
Only one out of every hundred people have this potential, so not everyone gets to 'stay'.
…… Well, there are those that have a natural ability to 'step up' this progress and become a vampire immediately, but this is so rare it's out of the question.
lines.mirror_moon:
"That's true, but things get complex from here.

lines.japanese:
「で、グールになったモノは死体であった頃の数年の歳月によって腐敗した自分の肉体を補うため、他の遺体の肉を食べる。
　そうして腐敗した肉体を元に戻して、ようやくゾンビ……生きる死体（リビングデッド）の仲間入りができるのよ」
「───ふうん。
じゃあそのリビングデッドっていうのが、さっきの『死者』ってヤツなんだ」
「まさか。
『死者』はただの人形よ。
リビングデッドは死者よりは格段に弱いけど、ちゃんと自分の意思と魂をもって活動する一人前の吸血種だもの。
操り死体にすぎない『死者』とはレベルが違うわ」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Once it becomes a ghoul, it eats the flesh of other corpses to replace the body that rotted during its years in the grave.
When its flesh has finally been restored, it joins the ranks of the zombies—the living dead.”
“───I see. So those living dead are the ‘Dead’ you were talking about?”
“Of course not. The Dead are only puppets. The living dead may be vastly weaker than the Dead, but they possess wills and souls of their own and act as full-fledged members of a vampiric species. They are nothing like the Dead, which are merely corpses pulled by strings.”
lines.mao_english:
“Once it becomes a ghoul, it eats the flesh of other corpses to replace the body that rotted during its years in the grave.
When its flesh has finally been restored, it joins the ranks of the zombies—the living dead.”
“───I see. So those living dead are the ‘Dead’ you were talking about?”
“Of course not. The Dead are only puppets. The living dead may be vastly weaker than the Dead, but they possess wills and souls of their own and act as full-fledged members of a vampiric species. They are nothing like the Dead, which are merely corpses pulled by strings.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"So, the dead bodies that became ghouls eat the flesh of other corpses in order to sustain their decayed body parts.
After restoring their bodies fully, they can become zombies…… members of the class of living corpses (The Living Dead)."
"---Hm.
So these Living Dead, is that the 'The Dead' from before?"
"Not at all.
"The Dead" are just puppets.
The Living Dead are much weaker than The Dead, but they are members of the vampire race with a will of their own.
They are a on a different level than those manipulated "Dead"."
lines.mirror_moon:
"So, the dead bodies that became ghouls eat the flesh of other corpses in order to sustain their decayed body parts.

lines.japanese:
「で、リビングデッドからさらに数年たって、人間としての知識を取り戻した者が吸血鬼、ヴァンパイヤと呼ばれる者達。
　ここまで残れる人間は一万人に一人ぐらい。
さっきもちらりと言ったけど、もって生まれた肉体に宿るポテンシャルが高いほど残れる確率は高くなるわ。
　このヴァンパイヤ達の生みの親となった一族の大本のヴァンパイヤをね、わたしたちは死徒と呼ぶの」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“After several more years, those living dead who regain the knowledge they possessed as humans become what people call vampires.
Only about one in ten thousand survives that far. As I mentioned, the greater the potential of the body one is born with, the better the odds.
We call the original vampire at the root of each bloodline—the progenitor of all those lesser vampires—a Dead Apostle.”
lines.mao_english:
“After several more years, those living dead who regain the knowledge they possessed as humans become what people call vampires.
Only about one in ten thousand survives that far. As I mentioned, the greater the potential of the body one is born with, the better the odds.
We call the original vampire at the root of each bloodline—the progenitor of all those lesser vampires—a Dead Apostle.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"And after many years, once a Living Dead is able to restore its intelligence, it becomes a vampire.
There's probably about only one out of every ten thousand who have this ability.
I said it before, but the more potential you have, the higher the success rate to stay.
We call the Dead Apostles the ones that make all these kinds of vampires."
lines.mirror_moon:
"And after many years, once a Living Dead is able to restore its intelligence, it becomes a vampire.
There's probably about only one out of every ten thousand who have this ability.
I said it before, but the more potential you have, the higher the success rate to stay.
We call the Dead Apostles the ones that make all these kinds of vampires."

lines.japanese:
「……やっぱりおかしいじゃないか。
そんな倍々ゲームじゃ化け物は増える一方だろ。
それじゃ今ごろ俺たちのまわりは吸血鬼で溢れてることになる」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish: “That still doesn’t add up. At that rate the monsters would multiply forever. The world ought to be crawling with vampires by now.”
lines.mao_english: “That still doesn’t add up. At that rate the monsters would multiply forever. The world ought to be crawling with vampires by now.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… That's still odd.
If this game goes on, then won't the world be overflowing with vampires eventually?"
lines.mirror_moon:
"…… That's still odd.
If this game goes on, then won't the world be overflowing with vampires eventually?"

lines.japanese:
「そうでもないわ。
死徒はね、自ら生み出したヴァンパイヤにいずれ討たれてしまうのよ。
　言ったでしょう？
　彼らは人間の真似事をしてるって。
死徒は娯楽のために、自らが吸い殺した人間に自らの血を分け与える。
　分け与えられた遺体は何万分の一という確率をくぐりぬけてヴァンパイヤに成長して、いずれ親である死徒を殺して、自らが新しい死徒になる。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Not necessarily. A Dead Apostle is eventually slain by one of the vampires it created.
I told you they imitate humans. Remember? For amusement, a Dead Apostle shares its blood with the humans it drains to death.
One corpse in tens of thousands survives the process and matures into a vampire; eventually that child kills its parent and becomes the new Dead Apostle.”
lines.mao_english:
“Not necessarily. A Dead Apostle is eventually slain by one of the vampires it created.
I told you they imitate humans. Remember? For amusement, a Dead Apostle shares its blood with the humans it drains to death.
One corpse in tens of thousands survives the process and matures into a vampire; eventually that child kills its parent and becomes the new Dead Apostle.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Not necessarily.
The Dead Apostles usually get killed by the new vampires they created.
Didn't I say it before?
They act like humans.
For their own enjoyment, they place their own blood inside the humans they preyed upon.
One out of tens of thousands of these corpses become vampires and eventually kill their parent vampires, becoming a new Dead Apostle themselves.
lines.mirror_moon:
"Not necessarily.
The Dead Apostles usually get killed by the new vampires they created.
Didn't I say it before?
They act like humans.
For their own enjoyment, they place their own blood inside the humans they preyed upon.

lines.japanese:
「騎士が武勲をたてて君主となり、やがて王を墜とすように────彼らもそういうゲームでもしなければ存在してられないの。
　……うん、理由はよくわからないけど、そうしないと退屈で死んじゃうんだって。
　悪魔的なるものの存在の軽さ、かな。
たとえ不老不死だとしても、存在意義がなければ空気と変わらないんだもの」
　バカみたいね、とアルクェイドは肩をすくめる。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Like a knight winning glory, becoming a lord, and finally overthrowing the king────they cannot bear to exist without games like that.
I do not really understand why, but apparently boredom would kill them otherwise.
Perhaps that is how little weight a demonic existence carries. Even an immortal amounts to no more than air without a reason to exist.”
Arcueid shrugs and calls it idiotic.
lines.mao_english:
“Like a knight winning glory, becoming a lord, and finally overthrowing the king────they cannot bear to exist without games like that.
I do not really understand why, but apparently boredom would kill them otherwise.
Perhaps that is how little weight a demonic existence carries. Even an immortal amounts to no more than air without a reason to exist.”
Arcueid shrugs and calls it idiotic.
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Like knights becoming lords through strength of arms, and killing the king----they can only survive by playing those sorts of games.
…… Yeah, I don't really understand why, but I guess that stops them from dying of boredom.
The whims of an existence close to a devil, I suppose.
Even if they are immortal, if they can't hold onto their meaning for existence, it is an empty immortality."
Arcueid remarks how silly it is as she slumps her shoulders.

lines.japanese:
「……そっか。
じゃあ、さっきアルクェイドが、その……始末した死者っていうのは死徒っていうヤツの兵士っていうわけなのか？」
「兵士というよりは人形ね。
本来なら血を吸われた人間が自力で吸血種として蘇生する過程を無視して、完全に死徒の分身として操られているものを死者と呼ぶの。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“I see. Then was that member of the Dead you disposed of one of a Dead Apostle’s soldiers?”
“More a puppet than a soldier. A corpse forced past the natural revival process and controlled entirely as an extension of a Dead Apostle is what we call one of the Dead.”
lines.mao_english:
“I see. Then was that member of the Dead you disposed of one of a Dead Apostle’s soldiers?”
“More a puppet than a soldier. A corpse forced past the natural revival process and controlled entirely as an extension of a Dead Apostle is what we call one of the Dead.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… I see.
Then, that Dead that you killed earlier…… that was something like a soldier of the Dead Apostles?"
"Not so much a soldier as a puppet.
The Dead Apostles control the dead bodies by skipping the process of becoming a vampire.
lines.mirror_moon:
"…… I see.
Then, that Dead that you killed earlier…… that was something like a soldier of the Dead Apostles?"
"Not so much a soldier as a puppet.
The Dead Apostles control the dead bodies by skipping the process of becoming a vampire.

lines.japanese:
「死者は親である死徒と繋がっているわ。
　死者だって自らが生存するためのエネルギーを必要とするから人間を襲い、肉をすする。
けど、その半分以上は親元である死徒に流れていくのよ。
　ようするに女王蜂を養う働き蜂みたいなものね。
　死者を操る死徒は、自分の棺の中で眠っているだけで力を蓄えてしまえるのよ」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“The Dead remain connected to the Dead Apostle that created them.
They need energy to persist, so they attack humans and gorge on flesh. More than half of what they consume flows back to their master.
Think of worker bees feeding a queen. A Dead Apostle that commands the Dead can gather strength while doing nothing but sleeping in its coffin.”
lines.mao_english:
“The Dead remain connected to the Dead Apostle that created them.
They need energy to persist, so they attack humans and gorge on flesh. More than half of what they consume flows back to their master.
Think of worker bees feeding a queen. A Dead Apostle that commands the Dead can gather strength while doing nothing but sleeping in its coffin.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
The Dead are completely connected to their parent vampire.
In order for them to survive, they attack others to eat their flesh, but more than half of that energy goes to their master.
Like a queen bee nourished by the worker bees, the Dead Apostles can use The Dead to increase their power while they sleep."

lines.japanese:
「……わたしの『敵』が簡単には見つからないのは、『敵』が死者を多く使っているから。
　あいつが自分の手を汚すのは一回だけ。
　あとは死者にした人間を操って、自分は眠っているだけで領地を広げていく。
―――通り魔殺人による遺体が何体も発見されてるって言うけど、あんなのは偽造に失敗しただけのものよ。
　実際、この街の犠牲者は百人をこえているわ。
　ひっそりと人知れずいなくなってしまっている人達の一部分が、あなたたちが騒いでいる犠牲者っていうことね」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“The reason my ‘enemy’ is so difficult to find is that it commands a great many of the Dead.
It only needs to dirty its own hands once.
After that, it controls the human it converted and expands its territory while it sleeps.
―――They say several victims of the serial killings have been discovered, but those were simply people whose transformation into one of the Dead failed.
In truth, more than a hundred people in this city have fallen victim.
The corpses everyone is making such a fuss over are only a fraction of all the people who quietly vanished without anyone ever knowing why.”
lines.mao_english:
“The reason my ‘enemy’ is so difficult to find is that it commands a great many of the Dead.
It only needs to dirty its own hands once.
After that, it controls the human it converted and expands its territory while it sleeps.
―――They say several victims of the serial killings have been discovered, but those were simply people whose transformation into one of the Dead failed.
In truth, more than a hundred people in this city have fallen victim.
The corpses everyone is making such a fuss over are only a fraction of all the people who quietly vanished without anyone ever knowing why.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"…… My 'enemy' can't be found easily because he's using a lot of The Dead.
He only dirties his hands once.
After that, he simply controls The Dead while he sleeps and expands his territory.
---They say many bodies are found in the recent supposed serial killings, but those are actually just failures.
To tell the truth, there are over a hundred victims in this city.
But only a small amount, the ones discovered, are the victims in the news."

lines.japanese:
「な――――」
　百人単位―――？
　その、吸血鬼に血を吸われて殺された人間がそんなにいるっていうのか？
　しかも、血を吸われた人間も同じように血を吸う化け物になって、さっきみたいに何気なく街を徘徊してるなんて―――
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Wh――――”
More than a hundred people―――?
Have that many people really been drained and killed by the vampire?
And have its victims become blood-drinking monsters themselves, wandering the streets as casually as that man―――

lines.mirrorMoon:
"Wha----"
Over a hundred---?
There are that many that had their blood sucked?
And all those people suck the blood of others to make them into monsters like themselves, like that wandering, lifeless thing earlier---
lines.mirror_moon:

lines.japanese:
「………ふざけ、てる」
　三日前。
　ホテルに泊まっていた人々が、それこそ何の意味もなく殺され尽くしたのを、思い出す。
　俺はあのホテルにいたけれど、その場面を見ていない。
だから言葉の上でしか想像できず、ソレがどんなに憎むべき暴力であったかを肌で感じ取れなかった。
　今だってそれは同じだ。
　人間の血を吸う吸血鬼がいて、そいつが少しずつ自分の領地を広げているなんて聞いても、実感はわかない。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“That is sick.”
Three nights ago.
I remember every guest in that hotel being slaughtered for no reason at all.
I had been in the hotel, but I had not witnessed the massacre itself. I could only imagine it in the abstract, unable to grasp firsthand how abhorrent that violence had been.
The same is true now.

Three days ago.

I was there but I didn't see it, so I can only visualize and can't really tell what kind of violence it was.
It's still the same.
I can't fathom the existence of vampires that suck human blood, just to increase their own territory.

lines.maoEnglish:

What would become of me if, without reason or warning, someone dearest to me were killed that way?
I do not want to imagine it, even for an instant.
I picture Akiha drained of blood and discarded like trash.
“Ghh――――”
What enrages me is―――that such a horror could happen at any moment in this city, and the complacency that kept me from noticing.

I don’t want to die―――just because someone is playing a game. It would be too bitter. It would be too meaningless.
To die with everything unfinished―――it would be unbearable.”

But at the very end, hadn’t there been something worse—a helpless grief that everything had been left unfinished?
That night, in the park.
A girl died simply because chance placed her there.
Nrvnqsr killed her before she even realized death was coming.

A lifetime severed without warning.
A death witnessed by no one.

I do not understand them either, and I have no desire to.
But if you insist on asking which side is evil, is it not the powerless one? In the end, the fault lies with whatever gets killed. A life unable to defend itself is destroyed—that is simply nature.”

　きっと、世界という最大の生物を殺してしまえるのは人間という種だけでしょうね」

Compensating for every natural weakness with things outside yourselves is, in a sense, proof of humanity's status as the strongest species.
Humanity may be the only species capable of killing the greatest living thing of all—the world itself.”

「けど人間は種としては優れている反面、一個の生命として考えると弱すぎる。
　自分たち以外のあらゆるものを犠牲にしなければ生きていけないなんていう弱さは、絶対的な『悪』に他ならないわ。
　知性の有無の違い、生態としての違いはあれ、あなたたちは何かを捕食することで生きている生物でしょう？
　なら―――殺す側の行為はいつだって正しいのよ。
罪があるとすれば、それはそのルールの中で生きているくせに自分を守れないあなた達のほうでしょう」
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“But while humanity is strong as a species, each individual life is terribly weak.
The inability to survive without sacrificing everything around you is nothing less than absolute evil.
Whatever the differences in intelligence or ecology, humans live by consuming other lives, do they not?
Then―――the act of killing is always right. If there is guilt, it belongs to you: you live under that rule, yet cannot defend yourselves within it.”

"But even though they are strong as a species, they are weak as individuals.
They can't live without sacrificing the lives of those not of their race, which is the ultimate 'evil', is it not?
It doesn't matter if they have intelligence or not, for you guys, everything is fair game for food, is it not?
So---the ones doing the killings are always right.
If there is a sin, then it is you guys not being able to protect yourself under that rule."

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: Arcueid argues that, whatever the differences in intelligence or ecology, human beings are organisms that survive by preying on something. mirror moon instead says that everything is 'fair game' for humans to eat. That turns a descriptive premise about life through predation into an assertion of indiscriminate moral permission immediately before her conclusion that the killer is always right.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: Living by predation becomes treating everything as fair game

We cannot even protect ourselves properly, so we gather together and keep one another alive; when something like you slips into that community―――we do not know what we can possibly do―――!”
“Yes. That is how humans defend themselves.
Because you are helpless once a superior species enters the herd, you created rules to keep such species outside it.
You are right, Shiki.
Under normal circumstances, what has happened in this city could never occur.”

Thud—I kicked the ground.
I am furious with myself for rejecting every argument, every sensible reason.
“Wh-what? Why are you suddenly angry, Shiki?”
“I am angry at how stupid I am! After everything I went through, why am I still trying to say something like this?”
Saying it aloud only makes my head spin worse.
I feel like such an idiot―――if there were a mirror nearby, I would smash it without hesitation.

「―――――え？」
　アルクェイドは呆然と俺の顔を見る。
　こっちはと言うと、ついに、というかやっと、というか、とにかく言いたい事をはっきりと口にして気分がようやく落ち着いてくれた。

“Idiot, isn’t it obvious?
This colossal fool named Shiki Tohno is trying to say he’ll help you until your body has healed!”
“―――――What?”
Arcueid stares at me in astonishment.
As for me, now that I have finally—at long last—forced out the words I meant to say, my turmoil begins to settle.

I look off in a completely different direction and make my voice as sour as possible.
“I can’t help it. You’re weak because of me, and I can’t ignore the monsters overrunning this city.
You’re too unreliable on your own in that condition, so I said I’d help—if you’re willing to settle for me.”

She keeps pumping my hand without letting go.

She looks truly, radiantly happy.

Once every member of the Dead in the city is gone, the parent vampire will have no choice but to emerge, so until then we hunt down the survivors.”
Her eyes fix on me. Is that all right?

Even knowing I’m hunting it, our enemy still has to send out the Dead to secure the bare minimum of food.”
―――Right. So that man was the one it sent out to secure the bare minimum of food.
“Exactly. So there’s no point searching any further tonight.”
lines.mirrorMoon:
"Basically.
But since this 'enemy' is a vampire, he needs to steal the blood and energy of others.
So, even though he knows I'm searching for them, he has to send The Dead out to get the minimal blood he needs."
---*sigh*
Then, the minimal Dead he sent out was that man from before, huh.

"So, searching further tonight will be useless, I think."

　アルクェイドは俺から手を離すと、タン、という軽い足取りでうしろに跳んだ。

“Vampire hunting is always tedious. We have to find my enemy’s coffin somewhere in this city. It was never going to end quickly.”

mirrorMoonErrors.reason: The Japanese closes Arcueid's dialogue after her promise that they will meet tomorrow, then narrates her dancing backward while watching Shiki. mirror moon never closes the quotation, so the displayed English presents the third-person stage direction as something Arcueid says aloud.
mirrorMoonErrors.title: A missing quotation mark makes narration part of Arcueid's farewell

lines.japanese:
「明日って―――ちょっと待て、待ち合わせ場所とかどうするんだよ、おい！」
「ここでいいよ。
時間は―――そうね、十時ごろがちょうどいいかな」
　笑顔で、実にかってに約束をする。
「おやすみなさい、志貴。
また明日、ここでね！」
　と。
　手をふって、アルクェイドは去っていった。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Tomorrow―――wait, where are we meeting?”
“Here is fine. As for the time―――ten o’clock should be about right.”
Smiling, she arranges the whole thing without consulting me.
“Good night, Shiki. I will see you here tomorrow!”
And with that.
Arcueid waves and leaves.

lines.japanese:
―――屋敷に帰ってきた。
　深夜ということもあって、屋敷の明かりは完全に消え去っている。
「………まずい、かな」
　屋敷の門に手をかける。
　がちん、という音。
　門には頑丈そうな錠が内側からかけられていた。
「―――まいったな。
切るわけにもいかないし」
　少し悩む。
　悩んでから、門を自力でよじのぼる事にした。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
―――I am back at the estate.
It is past midnight, and every light has gone out.
“This could be bad…”
I put a hand on the front gate.
Clang.
A sturdy lock has been fastened from inside.
“―――Wonderful. It is not as if I can cut through it.”
I think for a moment.
Then I decide to climb over under my own power.

I shouldn't cut this."

Then, I decide to climb over the gate.

lines.japanese:
……疲れた。
　ドロボウさんよろしくで門をよじ登って、玄関にたどり着く。
　門は鍵がかかっていたが、玄関の扉は開いていた。
「……翡翠、ちゃんと開けててくれたんだ」
　ほう、と感謝の吐息がもれる。
　秋葉や琥珀さんたちを起こさないように、抜き足で屋敷の中へと入っていった。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
I am exhausted.
After scaling the gate like a burglar, I reach the front entrance.
The gate is locked, but the front door has been left unlocked.
“Hisui remembered to leave it unlocked for me.”
I breathe out in gratitude.
Careful not to wake Akiha, Kohaku, or anyone else, I creep into the estate.

lines.mirrorMoon:
…… I'm exhausted.
After sneaking over the wall like a thief, I quietly make my way to the doorway.

So as not to wake Akiha, Kohaku-san or Hisui, I sneak my way through the mansion.

　一息ついて、ベッドに腰をかける。
「………………」
　アルクェイドとの約束。
　なんの因果か、また厄介なコトに足を踏み入れた遠野志貴。
「――――仕方ないじゃないか。
だってさ、放っておけなかったんだから」
　それとも、放っておきたくなかったのか。
lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“――――――Whew”
I catch my breath and sit down on the bed.
“…”
My promise to Arcueid.
And here is Shiki Tohno, by some twist of fate neck-deep in trouble again.
“――――I could not help it. I could not just leave her alone.”
Or perhaps I had not wanted to leave her alone.

lines.label: s142
lines.maoEnglish:
“Well, I suppose she is beautiful.”
I do not understand my own feelings.
Is this what it means to have no idea whether something is right or wrong?
Whatever the answer, I will be helping Arcueid again tomorrow.
For now, I will put every other thought aside, rest properly, and save my strength for tomorrow――――
